I'm working through a word placement problem on a 2D board where I need to place a contiguous sequence of symbols from a rack [B, D, D, G, G] to maximize newly placed symbols. The key constraints are: the overlapping cell must be isolated along the chosen axis (not already part of a word there), the sequence boundaries can't extend existing words, newly placed cells can't extend valid words on perpendicular axes, and after placement every maximal line touching the move must be valid. I'm trying to work out whether these constraints are consistent or if there's some tension between them.

The safest approach seems to be placing new cells with no perpendicular neighbors at all, so no perpendicular words form. For the overlapping cell, it would likely be part of a perpendicular word already (since it's occupied), but that word should remain valid since it existed before. Now I'm thinking about the geometry: if I fix one coordinate and vary the other, I can place a word along that axis. I need to find a line with exactly one existing cell surrounded by empty space, so I can build a word through that cell while keeping new tiles isolated perpendicular-wise. So I need to find an isolated cell with no occupied neighbors in any direction, then reuse it as an anchor point to extend a new word through empty space. Let me scan the board systematically, checking the column at b=-4 to see which cells are truly isolated and could serve as good reuse points for placing all five new tiles. I'm checking whether placing new cells along row a=19 would violate the rules. The key constraint is that perpendicular neighbors at a=18 are only occupied at b=-4 and b=13, so I can place new cells at other b values without creating forbidden adjacencies. But I also need to verify that the existing vertical line through b=-4 (which includes the reused cell) doesn't contain any forbidden three-letter sequences. I'm checking whether reusing the cell at (19,-4) is allowed under the rules—the existing vertical word runs along axis 0 while the new horizontal move uses axis 1, so there's no conflict. For the new horizontal word along row a=19, I need to ensure any new cells don't create unwanted vertical words with their neighbors, which means avoiding placement near b=13 where (18,b) is occupied.

The simplest approach is to place the reused G at the start of the horizontal word (b=-4) and add new tiles adjacent to it. This gives a 6-letter word starting with G, using the remaining tiles B, D, D, G, G in some order. I need to verify this forms a valid word with no forbidden 3-letter snippets and that the cells before and after the word are empty—which they are at (19,-5) and (19,2).

Now I'm checking which orderings of the remaining letters create valid words, starting by listing the forbidden triples that begin with G to eliminate invalid combinations. Now I'm systematically listing all the forbidden triples that use only B, D, and G letters, then I'll work through finding a valid arrangement of G, G, G, D, D, B that starts with G and avoids all these forbidden patterns.

I'm testing sequences like GGDB to see if they work, checking each consecutive triple against the forbidden list. When I place GGDB, the remaining letters G and D create problems—either DBG or BDG appears as the final triple, both of which are forbidden. So I'm backtracking and trying different starting patterns like GGB.

With GGB, I have {G,D,D} left to place. The triple GBG works, but then placing the remaining D's creates BGD as a triple, which is forbidden. Now I'm exploring starting with GD instead, which immediately restricts w3 to B since most letters are forbidden after GD. This gives me GDB, and continuing with the remaining {G,G,D}, I need w4 to avoid the forbidden DB combinations, forcing w4=D.

But then BDG appears as a forbidden triple with the remaining G's, so this path fails too. I'm realizing the letter combination {G,G,G,D,D,B} might be fundamentally constrained by the forbidden triples. Let me systematically check which triples among just these three letters are actually allowed. I'm testing different arrangements of the letters to find a valid sequence. Now I'm considering sequences that end with B to avoid problematic combinations, examining what letters can precede it. With w4w5w6 = GGB, I have G, D, D left for positions 1-3. Since w3w4w5 = w3GG must be allowed, w3 has to be D (DGG works, but GGG doesn't). That leaves w1w2 = {G,D}, and I need to check if w2w3w4 = w2DG is allowed.  If w2=D, then GDD for w1w2w3 is forbidden. If w2=G, then DGG for w1w2w3 works but GDG for w2w3w4 is forbidden. So position 6 can't hold B either.

Now I'm realizing that B creates a constraint: any allowed triple with B in the first position must have B in the third position too (BBB, BDB, BGB all end in B). Since there's only one B, it can't be at position 1 or 4 where it would start a triple. B can only go at position 5 or 6 to avoid being the first element of a complete triple.

If B is at position 5, then the triple (w3,w4,w5) ends in B and must be one of the allowed triples ending in B, while (w4,w5,w6) has B in the middle and must be either DBD or GBG (or variants like GBB/BBB).

Since w3GB must be an allowed triple ending in B, w3 must be G (making GGB), which means w1w2 are both D. Checking the sequence DDGGBG: all four consecutive triples (DDG, DGG, GGB, GBG) are allowed, and the letter counts are D×2, G×3, B×1.

Now I'm verifying that this word works with the reused cell. The word has G's at positions 3, 4, and 6, and the reused cell at (19,-4) is G. If I place the word along the b-axis starting at b=-6, the reused cell aligns with position 3 of the word (at b=-4). This means new tiles go at b=-6,-5,-3,-2,-1, and I need to check their perpendicular neighbors in rows 18 and 20 to ensure no unintended words form.

Row 18 only has occupied cells at b=-4 and b=13, so all the new cells have empty neighbors above. The word boundaries check out too—there's nothing at b=-7 or b=0 in row 19. The vertical line through the reused cell (column b=-4) runs along the a-axis and remains valid since it's not being reused along the chosen axis. Now I need to verify the remaining placement rules. The reused cell at (19,-4) is part of a vertical word, which is fine. None of the new cells at b=-6,-5,-3,-2,-1 overwrite existing cells—they're all empty. The move satisfies both requirements: reusing one existing cell and placing five new symbols from my rack. The score totals 8 points from the sequence D,D,G,G,B,G, and I'm placing all five rack symbols, which is the maximum possible.

Now I need to verify the word "DDGGBG" against the forbidden snippets by checking all length-3 substrings: DDG, DGG, GGB, and GBG are all valid—none appear in the forbidden list. The move is clean.

Let me also confirm the perpendicular constraint: the new cells at a=19 have no vertical neighbors at a=18 or a=20 that would create invalid words. The reused cell at (19,-4) already has its vertical word established along column b=-4, which doesn't interact with the new horizontal neighbors. And since row a=19 previously only contained the single cell at (19,-4), there's no existing horizontal word being extended. Everything checks out.

Now verifying the final move: start position [19,-6], axis 1 (advancing along the second coordinate), sequence DDGGBG. The cells placed are [19,-6] through [19,-1], with (19,-4) being reused with its existing symbol G matching index 2 of the sequence. The axis value is valid, and the entire sequence is accepted by the formal language. I'm verifying the vertical lines through each cell of the move to ensure no unintended words are created. The horizontal line at row 19 spans columns -6 to -1 with "DDGGBG" which is valid. For the vertical lines: (19,-6), (19,-5), and (19,-3) each stand alone as single cells with no adjacent tiles in their columns, so they're fine. The vertical through (19,-4) is the length-6 word I already validated. Everything checks out.
